findings.issue_text: Renamed files under packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/ only have imports updated for a subset of apps; basecamp3 and closecom (api/callback.ts, api/add.ts) still import old paths, causing module-not-found build failure and breaking those OAuth install flows

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:9-12 uses z.string().toString() computed keys which evaluate to the literal key '[object Object]', so the 'catch any expiry field' schema degenerates to an access_token-only check; requires catchall instead

refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token reads a property that does not exist on the schema's output type due to the broken wildcard pattern, causing TS2339 build error under strict mode or undefined at runtime

googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 stores the SafeParseReturnType wrapper from parseRefreshTokenResponse directly as the credential key instead of .data and never checks .success, so credential sharing would persist {success, data, error} garbage and break Google calendar sync
In googlecalendar CalendarService, when the sync endpoint is set, res is a fetch Response so res?.data is undefined and token.access_token throws

refreshOAuthTokens returns incompatible shapes across branches (fetch Response vs refreshFunction result) and axios/SDK-based callers were never adapted: zoho-bigin and zohocrm read tokenInfo.data (undefined on fetch Response) and hubspot expects a HubspotToken but receives a Response, crashing or persisting empty credentials when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set

salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-101 performs the new refresh fetch and prisma.credential.update unconditionally instead of gating on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, causing double refresh churn and new failure paths (e.g. transient refresh errors or missing consumer_secret) in default deployments

.env.example:241-243 contradicts itself: the comment says the key must be 32 bytes for AES256 but the suggested command 'openssl rand -base64 24' generates a 24-byte key, which can cause decryption failures at runtime

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParseReturn wrapper instead of .data, so Google Calendar credential keys get replaced with {success, data, error} on first token refresh, permanently breaking access_token/refresh_token lookups (P0)

In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the Google code reads res?.data and accesses token.access_token, throwing TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined on every Google token refresh with credential sync enabled (P0)

parseRefreshTokenResponse schema uses z.string().toString() keys evaluated at module load, producing duplicate literal string keys instead of a catch-all expiry matcher, so expiry fields (expires_in/expiry_date/expires_at) are never validated or captured in the sync path (P1)

When the parsed response lacks a refresh_token, parseRefreshTokenResponse fabricates the literal string 'refresh_token', which callers like office365 CalendarService persist to the DB, overwriting real refresh tokens with junk data (P1)

zoho-bigin CalendarService passes credentialId as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens instead of credential.userId, sending a credential row id as calcomUserId so the sync endpoint cannot match the right user (P2)

Salesforce CalendarService refresh block runs unconditionally at connection setup with no expiry check, no APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED gate, and no routing through refreshOAuthTokens, excluding Salesforce from credential sync and adding a token fetch + DB write on every instantiation (P1)

app-credential webhook reads the header name from CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME and uses it as-is against req.headers, but Node lowercases header names, so an env value with uppercase characters makes verification fail 100% of the time (P2)
app-credential webhook has no req.method check and uses schema.parse which throws, so GET/DELETE requests or malformed bodies produce a 500 with internal error details instead of 400/405 (P2)

app-credential webhook does findFirst-then-update/create without a transaction or unique constraint, so concurrent webhook deliveries for the same userId+appSlug both create duplicate Credential rows (P2)

HubSpot, Lark, and Zoho Bigin CalendarServices treat refreshOAuthTokens' sync-mode raw fetch Response as their original SDK/axios shape (reading expires_at, tokenInfo.data, etc.), causing NaN expiries or throws when sync is enabled, with no shared contract validating the sync endpoint response per app (P1)

.env.example key generation instructions are self-contradictory: requires a 32-byte key for AES256 but suggests 'openssl rand -base64 24' which generates 24 bytes, and no startup validation enforces either (P2)

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 replaces appConfig.slug-based redirect URI with hardcoded '/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback', a drive-by change that silently breaks OAuth if the slug diverges

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-99 adds an inline fetch to Salesforce's token endpoint plus unconditional prisma.credential.update instead of routing through refreshOAuthTokens, bypassing CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT and breaking credential-sharing mode

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:6-19 defines the pull-sync request/response contract only in a comment; no server for CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is implemented or specified in the diff

packages/lib/constants.ts:102-103 uses the single APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED flag to activate both receiver-side (webhook) and sender-side (pull) behavior, causing self-hosters who enable sharing to route their own token refreshes to an undefined sync endpoint, breaking all OAuth apps

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11 computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the static string '[object Object]', so the schema validates only access_token and silently strips expiry and other fields

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result wrapper, but googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-97 persists it directly as credential.key instead of .data, permanently corrupting the Google credential after the first refresh

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 fabricates refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = 'refresh_token' in sync mode; call sites persist this placeholder, overwriting the user's real refresh token and causing unrecoverable data loss
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts handles only create/update and has no revocation path, so credentials revoked on the parent remain valid indefinitely in the self-hosted database

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:12-18 pull request POSTs calcomUserId/appSlug with no auth header, signature, or shared contract, so the endpoint cannot verify the caller and the pull half of the feature is unimplementable
parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse wrapper object instead of .data, so Credential.key is persisted as the wrapper and Google Calendar auth breaks on next refresh

Zod computed keys z.string().toString() evaluate to literal '[object Object]', so minimumTokenResponseSchema silently strips all fields except access_token, causing expiry_date to be undefined and persisted
refreshOAuthTokens returns incompatible shapes (raw fetch Response vs parsed token object), breaking every caller like googlecalendar, zoho-bigin, and hubspot which expect a token body
Sync token refresh call in refreshOAuthTokens has no timeout, no response.ok check, and no fallback, causing cascading availability/booking failures when the sync endpoint is slow or down
app-credential webhook uses check-then-create (findFirst + create) with no UNIQUE(userId, appId, teamId) constraint, allowing concurrent webhooks to duplicate credentials
Placeholder 'refresh_token' sentinel string is persisted as credential.key, destroying the real refresh token and permanently breaking auth once credential sharing is disabled
Salesforce CalendarService performs unguarded token refresh + DB write on every service instantiation with no expiry check, bypassing refreshOAuthTokens and using a fragile statusText success check
.env.example documents 'openssl rand -base64 24' for a key that must be 32 bytes for AES-256, producing invalid key length errors at first decrypt

APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is exported as string | undefined treated as boolean, with the compound gate condition duplicated inline across call sites, risking drift and enabling sync with junk env values

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:91-97 — parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper instead of unwrapped .data, so the wrapper object is persisted as the credential key; the next googleCredentialSchema.parse on {success, error, data} strips/fails required fields, permanently breaking the Google Calendar credential until re-auth (P0)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:16-19 — when the sync endpoint returns only {access_token, expiry}, the code fabricates a fake refresh token (literal string 'refresh_token') and call sites overwrite the stored real refresh_token in the DB, making the credential impossible to refresh later if sync is disabled or breaks (P1)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5-21 — the abstraction returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode but provider-shaped objects in normal mode; zoho-bigin checks tokenInfo.data.error (undefined on a Response, so it writes undefined tokens/expiry into the credential) and hubspot annotates the result as HubspotToken but receives a Response, so unchanged downstream code reads provider fields off a Response object (P1)

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:91 — credentialId (the Credential row's id) is passed as the sync user ID instead of credential.userId, so the self-hoster's sync endpoint receives the wrong identifier and may resolve the wrong user or 404, potentially associating another user's app credentials with this credential row (P1)

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-98 — Salesforce performs an unconditional network token refresh + DB write on every service construction, bypassing refreshOAuthTokens entirely; this runs even when the token is valid and credential sharing is disabled, causing rate-limit/latency exposure on read paths and overwriting webhook-synced Salesforce credentials with the self-hoster's own refresh (P2)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-9 — the zod index-signature trick 'detect expiry via any numeric property' silently no-ops: z.string().toString() evaluates to '[object Object]', both computed keys collapse into one, and no expiry is enforced or extracted, leaving downstream expiry_date/expires_in handling operating on undefined (P2)

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:246-266 — the previous log-and-continue path for zod parse failures was deleted; parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' in both sync and non-sync branches, turning previously degraded-but-working MS token responses into hard failures of the booking/availability flow (P2)

packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:101-104 — the documented fallback sequence (TODO comment about initiating fallback instead of throwing) is now unreachable dead code because parseRefreshTokenResponse throws before parsedToken.success can ever be false, silently inverting the intended fallback behavior (P2)

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 - POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no auth header, signature, or shared secret, allowing anyone who can reach the endpoint to iterate sequential/guessable user IDs and harvest every synced user's OAuth credentials (unauthenticated cross-user credential disclosure / IDOR) — P1

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:7-9, 13-31 - Catch-all index signatures [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to '[object Object]', so minimumTokenResponseSchema is effectively {access_token: z.string()} and zod strips all other fields (expiry_date, refresh_token, instance_url), corrupting stored tokens

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts returns the SafeParseReturnType wrapper ({success, data}), and the Google caller CalendarService.ts:96-99 stores that wrapper verbatim into prisma.credential.update({data: {key}}), overwriting Google credentials with {success: true, data: {access_token}} and permanently losing refresh_token and expiry_date

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts - refresh_token = "refresh_token" placeholder is applied unconditionally, including in the non-sharing branch, so for providers whose refresh response omits refresh_token a real stored refresh token is overwritten with the literal string 'refresh_token'

app-credential.ts:31-35 - Non-constant-time comparison of the credential-write secret (req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET) plus no rate limiting; the single static secret gates prisma.credential.create/update against an arbitrary userId, enabling timing side-channel and unthrottled brute-force that grants arbitrary credential injection for any user — P2

zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:85-96 - Wrong identifier passed to credential sync: zoho-bigin passes a variable named credentialId while every other call site passes credential.userId, potentially causing the sync endpoint to return the wrong user's credentials and cross-user credential mix-up — P1, confidence 50, needs verification of credentialId's definition

refreshOAuthTokens returns incompatible shapes depending on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED branch: with sync enabled it returns a raw fetch Response instead of the adapter-specific token object, breaking HubSpot (hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token is undefined) and Zoho Bigin/CRM (tokenInfo.data.error is undefined so the error branch is never detected and expiryDate is computed from garbage)

googlecalendar CalendarService persists the safeParse result wrapper instead of the parsed data: assigning parseRefreshTokenResponse()'s return value (the wrapper, not .data) directly to the credential key column stores '{ success: true, data: {...} }' instead of the token object, corrupting every subsequently refreshed Google Calendar credential (unlike office365calendar which correctly consumes .success/.data)

parseRefreshTokenResponse's 'minimum token response' schema uses z.string().toString() as a catch-all key, which evaluates to the literal key '[object Object]', so the schema is not a wildcard: any valid token response lacking a property literally named '[object Object]' fails safeParse and throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', killing the user's calendar sync

salesforce CalendarService contains a dead Promise.reject at line 96 that is unreachable because parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws at line 88 for the same condition, and the two conflicting error-handling strategies go unverified
salesforce refresh flow strictly fails on response.statusText !== 'OK', which breaks in environments where statusText may be empty
Deleting the tolerant O365 behavior (console.error + continue-on-parse-failure in office365calendar CalendarService) makes the refresh flow strict-fail for office365 with no accompanying test change

The new credential-sharing logic (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse, app-credential webhook handler, Salesforce refresh path) has no test coverage: the sync branch's return-shape compatibility per app and the persisted prisma.credential.update payload shape are untested, and mock-based tests would validate nothing since existing suites are stale

In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:14-16, the catch-all schema keys use z.string().toString() which evaluates to the literal string '[object Object]', so the schema only retains access_token and a key named '[object Object]', stripping numeric properties like expiry_date; expiry-based logic (isExpired in lark, expiry_date checks in google/office365) then reads undefined after the first sync-write in credential-sharing mode

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, the refreshed credential parsed against minimumTokenResponseSchema has string fields (including refresh_token) stripped by zod, and the stripped result is written back via prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } }); in the Google path this permanently destroys the existing refresh_token stored in credential.key, requiring full re-authorization for Google/Office365/Zoom credentials (CalendarService.ts:96-99, office365 CalendarService.ts:266, zoomvideo VideoApiAdapter.ts:104)

In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:23-25, the code writes the literal placeholder string 'refresh_token' into the parsed object when no refresh_token is present, and this runs on both sharing and non-sharing paths; for apps whose schema lacks refresh_token, a previously-valid refresh token in the DB is overwritten with the placeholder and becomes permanently unusable

In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:60-93, the webhook replaces the locally-owned OAuth credential key with whatever the parent instance sends, with no backup, versioning, or validation of the decrypted key shape, causing one-way clobbering with no rollback path if the parent sends keys minted for its own OAuth client

In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, the findFirst + update/create pattern is not atomic, so two concurrent webhooks can create duplicate credential rows for the same user/app, and the later update fix-up path only corrects the first match

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the OAuth utility files were moved into `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/` and several apps (googlecalendar, hubspot, larkcalendar, office365, salesforce, etc.) had their imports updated accordingly. matched_golden_ids: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same underlying bug: in sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response without a .data property, but the code reads res?.data and then token.access_token, causing a TypeError due to undefined. This matches the golden comment’s concern about inconsistent return shape and runtime failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse schema uses z.string().toString() keys evaluated at module load, producing duplicate literal string keys instead of a catch-all expiry matcher, so expiry fields (expires_in/expiry_date/expires_at) are never validated or captured in the sync path (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. In JS/TS, computed property names are evaluated immediately at module load, and `z.string().toString()` produces a fixed literal string (not a “match any key” pattern). That makes the schema require a property with that exact literal key (and a number value), so typical OAuth token responses with `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, etc. will not satisfy the schema. Therefore, in the credential-sync path (where this minimum schema is used), `safeParse` will fail and throw, and the intended expiry-field handling does not work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When the parsed response lacks a refresh_token, parseRefreshTokenResponse fabricates the literal string 'refresh_token', which callers like office365 CalendarService persist to the DB, overwriting real refresh tokens with junk data (P1)
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: parseRefreshTokenResponse assigns the literal string 'refresh_token' when the field is absent, leading to persistence of an invalid token and breaking future refresh/auth flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: zoho-bigin CalendarService passes credentialId as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens instead of credential.userId, sending a credential row id as calcomUserId so the sync endpoint cannot match the right user (P2)
matched_golden_ids: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same bug: CalendarService passes a credential row ID (credentialId) into refreshOAuthTokens where a userId (credential.userId) is expected, leading to incorrect user matching/lookup and broken sync behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService refresh block runs unconditionally at connection setup with no expiry check, no APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED gate, and no routing through refreshOAuthTokens, excluding Salesforce from credential sync and adding a token fetch + DB write on every instantiation (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows the beginning of `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` changes: adding `zod`, importing `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, and defining `salesforceTokenSchema`. It does not include (or show modifications to) the actual connection setup / refresh-token logic, any DB writes, or whether refresh is unconditional or gated by expiry / `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` / `refreshOAuthTokens`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential webhook reads the header name from CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME and uses it as-is against req.headers, but Node lowercases header names, so an env value with uppercase characters makes verification fail 100% of the time (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the code indexes `req.headers` with `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` directly: `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]`. In Node/Next.js, incoming header names are normalized to lowercase in `req.headers`, so if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is set with any uppercase characters (e.g., `Calcom-Webhook-Secret`), this lookup will return `undefined` and the secret check will always fail. The diff even comments "Should be in lowercase" but does not enforce/lowercase it, making this a real, verifiable correctness/operational bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential webhook has no req.method check and uses schema.parse which throws, so GET/DELETE requests or malformed bodies produce a 500 with internal error details instead of 400/405 (P2)

This matches the golden issue about `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` throwing on invalid payloads and causing 500s. adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential webhook does findFirst-then-update/create without a transaction or unique constraint, so concurrent webhook deliveries for the same userId+appSlug both create duplicate Credential rows (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` and then conditionally calls `update` or `create`. This is a classic non-atomic read-then-write pattern: two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same `(userId, appSlug/appId)` can both see “no row” and both execute `credential.create(...)`, producing duplicates if the DB allows it. Even if a unique constraint exists, this code doesn’t handle the resulting unique-violation error, so concurrent deliveries can still fail unpredictably. No transaction or `upsert` is used here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/constants.ts:102-103 uses the single APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED flag to activate both receiver-side (webhook) and sender-side (pull) behavior, causing self-hosters who enable sharing to route their own token refreshes to an undefined sync endpoint, breaking all OAuth apps

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11 computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the static string '[object Object]', so the schema validates only access_token and silently strips expiry and other fields

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, the object shape uses computed property names `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()`. Those expressions are evaluated immediately to a plain string (not a pattern/dynamic key), so they do not create “any key with number value” / “any other key” behavior. In practice both computed keys collapse to a single static property name (e.g. `"[object Object]"`), and Zod will not preserve arbitrary fields like `expiry_date`; unknown keys are stripped by default. So when `safeParse(response)` succeeds, `refreshTokenResponse.data` will effectively only contain `access_token` (and maybe that one accidental key), causing expiry/other fields to be dropped and not propagated to callers that rely on `.data`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result wrapper, but googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-97 persists it directly as credential.key instead of .data, permanently corrupting the Google credential after the first refresh

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the result of zod.safeParse(...) (a wrapper object with { success, data, error }), not the parsed credential object itself. In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code assigns `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists `{ key }` via `prisma.credential.update(...)`. This would store the safeParse wrapper into credential.key instead of the actual credentials (e.g., key.success/key.data), which is a concrete correctness bug that would corrupt the stored credential shape after a refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 fabricates refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = 'refresh_token' in sync mode; call sites persist this placeholder, overwriting the user's real refresh token and causing unrecoverable data loss
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts handles only create/update and has no revocation path, so credentials revoked on the parent remain valid indefinitely in the self-hosted database

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts only supports upserting (findFirst + update/create) a credential record. There is no explicit delete/revocation endpoint or logic in this diff, but the finding’s claim that this causes “credentials revoked on the parent [to] remain valid indefinitely” is not directly verifiable from the diff: no parent revocation mechanism, contract, or expected behavior is shown, and credential invalidation could be handled externally (e.g., provider-side revocation, parent refusing refresh via CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, or sending updated/empty keys). Thus it’s a speculative feature-gap assumption rather than a clear defect introduced by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens.ts:12-18 pull request POSTs calcomUserId/appSlug with no auth header, signature, or shared contract, so the endpoint cannot verify the caller and the pull half of the feature is unimplementable

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, the code performs a `fetch` POST that sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body via `URLSearchParams` and does not include any authentication material (no header, signature, token, or secret). Nothing in this diff shows an alternative mechanism for the remote endpoint to authenticate/verify the caller based on the request contents, so a reviewer can reasonably flag this as a real security/contract defect in the introduced sync flow (even if “unimplementable” is overstated, the missing auth is verifiable).

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse wrapper object instead of .data, so Credential.key is persisted as the wrapper and Google Calendar auth breaks on next refresh

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function returns the `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error }`) rather than `refreshTokenResponse.data`. However, in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the result is assigned to `key` and persisted as `credential.key` via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Previously this code stored the parsed credential object (`googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`). Persisting the Zod wrapper instead of the credential data is a concrete type/shape change that will corrupt the stored credential payload and can break subsequent reads/refresh logic that expects `credential.key` to be the credential fields.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zod computed keys z.string().toString() evaluate to literal '[object Object]', so minimumTokenResponseSchema silently strips all fields except access_token, causing expiry_date to be undefined and persisted

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `minimumTokenResponseSchema` as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), ... })`. In JS/TS, `z.string()` is a ZodString object, so `.toString()` will produce the string `"[object Object]"`, meaning the schema is defining a *literal* property named `"[object Object]"`, not a dynamic/index signature. Zod `z.object(...)` will then require that property to exist (and by default strips unknown keys), so real token responses (with fields like `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, etc.) will not match and `safeParse` will fail, causing `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to throw `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"` when credential sharing is enabled. The proposed finding’s specific claim about “silently strips all fields except access_token” is not quite right (it will more likely fail validation outright), but the underlying issue (computed keys become `"[object Object]"` and the schema won’t accept expiry fields) is a real defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens returns incompatible shapes (raw fetch Response vs parsed token object), breaking every caller like googlecalendar, zoho-bigin, and hubspot which expect a token body

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns two different shapes depending on config: when sharing is enabled it returns the result of `fetch(...)` (a standard Fetch `Response`), but otherwise it returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns (often a parsed token object or a library-specific response). This is verifiably incompatible with at least the Google Calendar caller: it does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` which works for `myGoogleAuth.refreshToken(...).res` (GaxiosResponse with `.data`), but will be `undefined` for a Fetch `Response` (no `.data` field). Therefore token parsing/updating will break when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set. Similar risk exists for Hubspot where the variable is typed as `HubspotToken` but could become a Fetch `Response` under the sharing path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sync token refresh call in refreshOAuthTokens has no timeout, no response.ok check, and no fallback, causing cascading availability/booking failures when the sync endpoint is slow or down

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `refreshOAuthTokens` unconditionally calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). That code has (1) no timeout/abort mechanism, so the request can hang, (2) no `response.ok` / status validation before returning, and (3) no try/catch to fall back to the provided `refreshFunction` if the sync endpoint errors or is unavailable. Since multiple Calendar/Video services now route token refresh through this helper, failures/latency of the sync endpoint will directly propagate into token refresh flows rather than gracefully degrading. This is a concrete behavior introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential webhook uses check-then-create (findFirst + create) with no UNIQUE(userId, appId, teamId) constraint, allowing concurrent webhooks to duplicate credentials

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler does perform a non-atomic "check then create" sequence (`findFirst` then `create`) for credentials keyed by `{ userId, appId }`, which can race under concurrent requests. However, the proposed finding’s core claim—“with no UNIQUE(userId, appId, teamId) constraint, allowing duplicates”—is not verifiable from this diff: the Prisma schema / DB constraints are not shown here, and the handler doesn’t involve `teamId` at all. Without evidence of missing uniqueness constraints, duplication is only a potential issue, not a confirmed defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Placeholder 'refresh_token' sentinel string is persisted as credential.key, destroying the real refresh token and permanently breaking auth once credential sharing is disabled
Salesforce CalendarService performs unguarded token refresh + DB write on every service instantiation with no expiry check, bypassing refreshOAuthTokens and using a fragile statusText success check
.env.example documents 'openssl rand -base64 24' for a key that must be 32 bytes for AES-256, producing invalid key length errors at first decrypt

adjudication_records.issue_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is exported as string | undefined treated as boolean, with the compound gate condition duplicated inline across call sites, risking drift and enabling sync with junk env values

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` being imported and used in boolean contexts, and the same compound condition (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT ...`) appears in multiple new helpers/call sites. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:91-97 — parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper instead of unwrapped .data, so the wrapper object is persisted as the credential key; the next googleCredentialSchema.parse on {success, error, data} strips/fails required fields, permanently breaking the Google Calendar credential until re-auth (P0)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file) returns the full Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error }`), not `data`. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code was changed from `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials);` to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists `key` via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That means the persisted credential `key` will now be the SafeParse wrapper rather than the expected credential payload object, which is a concrete correctness bug introduced by this diff and would break downstream code that expects `credential.key` to directly contain Google credential fields.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:16-19 — when the sync endpoint returns only {access_token, expiry}, the code fabricates a fake refresh token (literal string 'refresh_token') and call sites overwrite the stored real refresh_token in the DB, making the credential impossible to refresh later if sync is disabled or breaks (P1)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, if the parsed token payload lacks `refresh_token`, it sets `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token". In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` and then merges `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` via `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`, which will overwrite the previously stored real `refresh_token` with the fabricated placeholder when the sync endpoint returns only `access_token`/expiry. That merged object is then used in a subsequent `prisma.credential.update(...)` (shown immediately after), so the DB-stored credential can be corrupted, breaking later refreshes if sync is disabled or fails. (Note: this overwrite is clearly true for the Office365 path in the diff; other call sites like Google pass an object that already contains the refresh_token, so they wouldn’t trigger the fabrication.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5-21 — the abstraction returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode but provider-shaped objects in normal mode; zoho-bigin checks tokenInfo.data.error (undefined on a Response, so it writes undefined tokens/expiry into the credential) and hubspot annotates the result as HubspotToken but receives a Response, so unchanged downstream code reads provider fields off a Response object (P1)

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-98 — Salesforce performs an unconditional network token refresh + DB write on every service construction, bypassing refreshOAuthTokens entirely; this runs even when the token is valid and credential sharing is disabled, causing rate-limit/latency exposure on read paths and overwriting webhook-synced Salesforce credentials with the self-hoster's own refresh (P2)

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-9 — the zod index-signature trick 'detect expiry via any numeric property' silently no-ops: z.string().toString() evaluates to '[object Object]', both computed keys collapse into one, and no expiry is enforced or extracted, leaving downstream expiry_date/expires_in handling operating on undefined (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts the `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is built with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. `z.string()` returns a Zod schema object, so `.toString()` yields a string like `"[object Object]"` (not an index signature). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:246-266 — the previous log-and-continue path for zod parse failures was deleted; parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' in both sync and non-sync branches, turning previously degraded-but-working MS token responses into hard failures of the booking/availability flow (P2)

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:7-9, 13-31 - Catch-all index signatures [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to '[object Object]', so minimumTokenResponseSchema is effectively {access_token: z.string()} and zod strips all other fields (expiry_date, refresh_token, instance_url), corrupting stored tokens

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, the computed keys use `z.string().toString()` / `z.string().optional().toString()` as object property names. Those expressions evaluate to a single string at runtime (very plausibly `"[object Object]"`), meaning they do not act as “catch-all” index signatures. In fact, both computed keys likely collapse to the same property name, with the latter overwriting the former. As a result, the schema is effectively just `{ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]"?: z.unknown() }`. Zod `object()` also strips unknown keys by default, so fields like `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `refresh_token`, `instance_url`, etc. will be dropped from `refreshTokenResponse.data`. This can break token refresh logic: e.g., `Office365CalendarService` relies on merging parsed refresh response data into credentials, but `expires_in`/expiry info would be removed; and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` then forces a fake `refresh_token` when missing, further corrupting stored credentials.

app-credential.ts:31-35 - Non-constant-time comparison of the credential-write secret (req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET) plus no rate limiting; the single static secret gates prisma.credential.create/update against an arbitrary userId, enabling timing side-channel and unthrottled brute-force that grants arbitrary credential injection for any user — P2

adjudication.rationale: The new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` gates credential creation/update solely on a single shared secret: it compares `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and, if it matches, proceeds to `prisma.credential.update/create` for whatever `userId` is provided in the request body. There is no additional authentication/authorization tying the caller to that `userId`, and no throttling/rate limiting shown in the handler. The secret check uses normal JS `!==` string comparison (not constant-time), so in principle it is not timing-safe. Thus, if the secret is guessed/brute-forced (made more feasible by lack of rate limiting), the endpoint allows arbitrary credential injection/overwrite for any userId.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the new `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, it does `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object. In the else-branch it returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns (e.g., HubSpot’s `HubspotToken` object from `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken`, or Google’s `myGoogleAuth.refreshToken(...).res` which is then read via `res.data`). In the diff, HubSpot now assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`; under the sync-enabled branch that value would actually be a `Response`, so properties like `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token`/`expires_in` will be `undefined` and downstream logic will break. This is a concrete, diff-verifiable return-shape incompatibility introduced by `refreshOAuthTokens`.

In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:60-93, the webhook replaces the locally-owned OAuth credential key with whatever the parent instance sends, with no backup, versioning, or validation of the decrypted key shape, causing one-way clobbering with no rollback path if the parent sends keys minted for its own OAuth client

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler decrypts `reqBody.keys` and immediately `JSON.parse`s it, then writes it straight into `credential.key` via `update`/`create` without any schema/shape validation of the decrypted payload (it’s effectively `any`). If a credential already exists for that `userId` + `appId`, it is unconditionally overwritten (no merge, backup, versioning, or rollback mechanism in this code path). That one-way clobbering behavior is directly visible in lines 60–93. The specific scenario about “keys minted for its own OAuth client” is contextual, but the underlying risk (accepting and overwriting with unvalidated remote key material) is real in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, the findFirst + update/create pattern is not atomic, so two concurrent webhooks can create duplicate credential rows for the same user/app, and the later update fix-up path only corrects the first match

adjudication.rationale: The webhook handler does a classic check-then-act sequence: it `findFirst` for an existing `credential` by `{ userId, appId }`, then either `update` that row or `create` a new one. This is not atomic and is not wrapped in a transaction or Prisma `upsert`. Two concurrent requests for the same user/app can both observe “no credential” and both attempt `create`, which can either (a) produce duplicate rows if there is no unique constraint on `(userId, appId)`, or (b) cause one request to throw on a uniqueness violation (there is no error handling). Additionally, if duplicates exist for any reason, `findFirst` + `update` will only update an arbitrary first match, leaving other rows unchanged.
